rules.message: Page titles go through PageHeader — never a bare <h1> in a page body (PLACEMENT.md, Header slots).
Use the DS table primitives, not a raw <table> (gate 2 of the four-gate stack).
Use the Button primitive, not a bare <button> (gate 2 of the four-gate stack).
Use semantic tokens (bg-muted, text-muted-foreground, Badge variant), not a literal Tailwind palette class (audit-signals: literal-color).
Use focus-visible:ring-2 ring-ring (audit-signals: weak-focus-ring).
Use the shadcn atom — Input / Select / Textarea (audit-signals: raw-html-control).

A prop named from the appearance-noun list is a per-call-site appearance the contract does not derive (RULES.md hard rule 12). Closed archetypes (detail-overview, form-page, list-with-detail, settings-table) are gated by their own `*-` error rules. Excluded: entity-circle — its `tone` is contract-keyed to the entity's identity role (entity-circle.md L7: brand tone reserved for the signed-in identity; every other entity is neutral), so ADR-0004's derived test passes and the prop is legal; its `size` is contract-keyed to the scope of the thing the entity is the subject of (entity-circle.md L6: attribute of the surrounding row/cell -> xs, subject of its own row or list item -> sm, subject of the whole surface -> md; an omitted size resolves to sm, the rule's answer for that scope), so the optional prop is legal. `size` is in this rule's pattern so a future archetype that grows one is flagged. Excluded: calendar — its `tone` is contract-keyed to the event's domain status (calendar.md Layer 7: failed/blocked/overdue -> warning, completed/confirmed -> success, noteworthy/externally-driven -> info, no domain status -> default, and the shell resolves an omitted tone to default — the rule's answer for no status, so the optional prop is legal). The `include` carries `src/components/layout/**` as a second root (same shape as `archetype-numeric-union-prop`) because the shared chrome the archetype shells compose (`SectionCard`, `SurfaceFrame`) lives outside `src/components/archetypes/` — hard rule 12 governs an appearance prop on an archetype composition regardless of which directory owns it, and without the root a closed archetype could forward a prop it is supposed to fully key to an ungated owner one directory over (detail-overview's `DetailSection.tone` -> `SectionCard.tone`). Excluded: `SectionCard.tsx` — its `tone` is contract-keyed to the section's role on the page (detail-overview.md:517-519, surface grading: data sections -> the default tone, reference panels -> `tone="muted"`; the "three weights" of that sentence count the separately-governed stat strip as the third, not a third `tone` value), so ADR-0004's derived test passes and the prop is legal.

A prop typed as an inline string-literal union of look-names is a design space two projects can fill differently (RULES.md hard rule 12). Closed archetypes (detail-overview, form-page, list-with-detail, crud-dialog, settings-table) are gated by their own `*-` error rules. Excluded: report — its `width` union is contract-keyed to the document's shape (report.md Structure, width keying rule: compact receipt / short Beleg -> sm, standard document column -> md, wide statement with many columns -> lg), so ADR-0004's derived test passes and the prop is legal. The `include` carries `src/components/layout/**` as a second root (same shape as `archetype-numeric-union-prop`) because the shared chrome the archetype shells compose (`SectionCard`, `SurfaceFrame`) lives outside `src/components/archetypes/` — hard rule 12 governs an appearance prop on an archetype composition regardless of which directory owns it. Excluded: `SectionCard.tsx` — its `tone` union is contract-keyed to the section's role on the page (detail-overview.md:517-519, surface grading: data sections -> the default tone, reference panels -> `tone="muted"`), so ADR-0004's derived test passes and the prop is legal; see `archetype-appearance-noun-prop`, which owns the same prop's triage under its noun pattern. Excluded: `SurfaceFrame.tsx` — its `overflow` union is contract-keyed to whether the bounded surface holds a sticky-edge grid (matrix-grid.md Layer 5, overflow keying rule: nothing pinned during horizontal scroll -> clipped, a grid with a sticky first column -> the surface IS the scroll container, because a sticky cell stays pinned only while the element it scrolls inside is the surface itself), so ADR-0004's derived test passes and the prop is legal. Excluded: `ProgressTracker.tsx` — its `ProgressStep.state` (`"done" | "current" | "pending"`) is a DOMAIN-STATE union on a data-item type, not a look: the value comes from the step's position in the lifecycle the caller is rendering, and the component maps each state to a fixed token treatment (see its visual contract) with no per-call-site choice left over — ADR-0004's derived test passes because nothing about it is inherited from the call site. Excluded: `tableColumn.ts` — its `align` is contract-keyed to the column's value kind (settings-table.md:143-149, Layer 6 keying rule: numerical / monetary / date / count figures -> `right`, status / category / toggle / identifier / categorical badge (short token) -> `center`, everything else -> `left` (default); the shared contract decision list-with-detail adopts), so ADR-0004's derived test passes and the prop is legal. This rule's pattern reaches every inline string union, so a data union in a row/item type lands here and is triaged, not deleted. The pattern also allows an optional container OPENERS prefix (`Array<` / `ReadonlyArray<` / `Readonly<`, a `readonly (…)`, or an opening paren before the union) so a union wrapped in a per-item container is this one rule's job across every spelling — `Array<Readonly<"default" | "strong">>`, `readonly ("left" | "center" | "right")[]`, `("a" | "b")[]` — reported once under this same message (the `^\s*` anchor guarantees one hit per line, so the widening cannot double-report); the prefix only consumes OPENERS, so a container of a non-union element (`string[]`, `React.ReactNode[]`) is never matched. Excluded: `shared/FigureTable.tsx` — its three per-cell look-vector props (`emphasis?: Array<Readonly<"default" | "strong">>`, and `cellAlign` / `headerAlign?: readonly ("left" | "center" | "right")[]`) are index-aligned per-cell STYLING DATA on a data row, not shell appearance: the value comes from the row's own kind (statement-with-filters.md Layer 6, the totals row — its figures render `strong`, and `emphasis` is set only by the total-row wrapper, so its value is derived from the row being a total; report.md L56, the line-item table — name sans + qty/unit/sum figures, the qty column centered, the one `cellAlign` / `headerAlign` value the report keys it to), so two engineers holding the same statement or report derive the same vector and ADR-0004's derived test passes. An index-aligned per-cell vector of a data row is the SAME nested-styling-data category the `archetype-shell-class-name` and `archetype-appearance-boolean-prop` rules' indent-≤2 cap deliberately spares (the matrix-grid per-cell `cellStyle` precedent cited in `archetype-shell-class-name`'s message), not the shell's outer wrapper — it is excluded here by that not-shell-appearance reasoning, not deleted, because every value it can render is fixed by the component once the vector is given.

A prop typed as a bare numeric-literal union (`columns?: 2 | 3 | 4`) is the same per-call-site appearance axis as a string-literal look union — the quoted-string pattern of `archetype-look-union-prop` only reaches quoted members and never matches it (RULES.md hard rule 12). The `include` carries `src/components/layout/**` as a second root because the shared chrome (`StatTileRow`) lives outside `src/components/archetypes/`. Closed archetypes (detail-overview, form-page, list-with-detail, crud-dialog, settings-table, report) are gated by their own `*-` error rules. Excluded: statement-with-filters — its `StatementRow.indent` is contract-keyed to the row's own depth in the statement's group -> children data, capped at 2 (statement-with-filters.md Layer 6, indent keying rule: top-level row (no parent group) -> 0, child of a top-level group -> 1, grandchild or deeper -> 2, the terminal step), so ADR-0004's derived test passes and the prop is legal. Excluded: analytics-dashboard — its `DashboardWidget.span` is contract-keyed to the widget's kind (analytics-dashboard.md Layer 6, widget span keying rule: primary trend -> full width, comparison/breakdown -> wide, everything else -> one column) and carries no default, so ADR-0004's derived test passes and the prop is legal. Its deleted `columns` props are separately gated by the `analytics-dashboard-columns-prop` / `stat-tile-row-columns-prop` error rules.

A prop typed against a union type ALIAS (`circleSize?: EntityAvatarSize`) is the same per-call-site design space as an inline look union, just named once (RULES.md hard rule 12). `{{unionAliases}}` is substituted per scanned file with the union aliases that file itself declares (scripts/lint-design.mjs `harvestUnionAliases`) — same-file only, no type resolution (ADR-0003). The leading negative lookahead skips the appearance-noun prop names `archetype-appearance-noun-prop` already owns — its alternation is that rule's owned-noun set verbatim (surface, variant, tone, density, appearance, rhythm, fill, framed, bordered, compact, padded, size) and must be kept identical to it — so an aliased noun prop is reported once, by that rule under its per-archetype triage, not twice under two different messages. That is why entity-circle is absent from the `exclude` below: its `size?: EntityAvatarSize` is skipped by the lookahead, so the noun rule's entity-circle triage is the single place the decision lives. Closed archetypes (detail-overview, form-page, list-with-detail, crud-dialog, settings-table, report) are gated by their own `*-` error rules. Excluded: overline-typed — its `as?: OverlineElement` selects the rendered ELEMENT, not a look: the contract keys it to the document outline (overline-typed.md L8 — the element it renders as is selectable because a label above a heading may be a non-heading element or may itself be the section heading; L11 — when the overline IS the semantic section heading it renders as the heading element so the document outline stays correct), so it is not an appearance axis at all. Excluded: raw-input — its `type?: NativeFieldType` selects the native input TYPE, not a look: the contract keys it to the field's data kind (raw-input.md:39 — the enumerated native controls the field assembles: text, number, date/time, password/url/email, a `range` slider, multi-line text) and to the platform keyboarding each of those carries (L4:77–78 — the native control keeps its native keyboarding verbatim: a date control's picker, a range control's arrow-key stepping, a textarea's newline), so it is not an appearance axis at all.

A boolean look FLAG is a per-call-site appearance the contract does not derive — the same design space as an appearance-noun prop or a look union, just spelled as an on/off (RULES.md hard rule 12). A boolean is disqualified twice over when its default is off: ADR-0004 — "A backwards-compatible default is disqualifying on its own. It means the value was inherited rather than derived." The vocabulary is an ALLOWLIST, mirroring how `archetype-appearance-noun-prop`'s noun list was chosen: behaviour/capability booleans (`isLoading`, `bulkSelectable`, `sortable`, `unread`, `chrome`, `canDelete`, `showDestructive`, `showSidebarTrigger`) are kept out at the pattern level, not excluded one by one, because a capability is not an appearance. `show*`/`hide*` are therefore NOT wildcards — only the three live look toggles (`hideCount`, `showHeader`, `showCount`) are named, so `showDestructive` (a permission) and `showSidebarTrigger` (a shell-composition fact) never enter this rule's scope. The appearance nouns that are already boolean-shaped (`framed`, `bordered`, `compact`, `padded`) are deliberately ABSENT: `archetype-appearance-noun-prop` owns those names whatever their type, and one prop name gets one owner — the same double-ownership discipline `archetype-alias-union-prop`'s negative lookahead enforces. `include` carries `src/components/layout/**` as a second root because the shared chrome the archetype shells compose lives there (`MetricList`, `SectionCard`) and no appearance-prop rule reached it. Closed folders are NOT excluded here: the per-folder ratchet rules ban deleted props by name and none of them names a boolean, so a closed archetype's boolean flags are only gated by this rule. Excluded: `MetricList.tsx` — its `emphasis` is contract-keyed to the metric's tier (detail-overview.md:205-207: the compact metric readout is "a condensed, ruled metric list (label left, tabular value right, a 'show more' disclosure for secondary figures)" — two tiers, headline rows and secondary figures, and `emphasis` renders the headline tier; the discretionary `accent` on the same primitive was deleted, not excluded). Excluded: `SectionCard.tsx` and `DetailSection.tsx` — their `flush` is contract-keyed to the content kind (detail-overview.md:512: "ruled row lists use `flush` (rows own their own padding and hairline dividers); free-form content (islands, prose) omits it and gets the section's default padding"). Excluded: `TextareaField.tsx` — its `mono` is contract-keyed to the field's data kind (raw-textarea.md:92: "mono / code (allowed variation) — a monospace tone for JSON/config input, which also disables spell-check"), the same not-an-appearance-axis reasoning `archetype-alias-union-prop` applies to raw-input's `type`. Excluded: `ListSkeleton.tsx` — its `showHeader` and `avatar` are contract-keyed to the shape being mirrored (skeleton-loader.md:35: "The placeholder can mirror that shape, so the layout doesn't jump"; :75-78 enumerate `header` and `leading media` as the shape knobs, the latter "for row shapes that lead with one"), so both are derived from the real list, not chosen per call site. Excluded: `tableColumn.ts` — its `identifierMono` is contract-keyed to the identifier's character style (list-with-detail.md:170 / settings-table.md:142: the monospace identifier style is set via `identifierMono: true`, off by default, for alphanumeric-code / slug identifiers, and omitted for human-readable name identifiers — both readers of the same column config derive the same value), so ADR-0004's derived test passes and the flag is legal. A path `exclude` un-gates the whole FILE, not the one legal prop — that ceiling is the same one every per-archetype exclude in this config carries, and tightening it to a per-file allowlist is `adherence-lint-closed-folder-allowlist-gap`'s mechanism, not a second one invented here.

`className` is an unenumerable superset escape hatch on a shell's outer wrapper — fork the component instead (RULES.md hard rule 12). The pattern stops at the `:` and does NOT pin the type: `className?: ClassValue` (already idiomatic in this repo — `src/components/layout/SurfaceFrame.tsx`) is the same escape hatch as `className?: string`, so pinning `\s*string` let a shell reopen the deleted axis by widening the annotation. Scoped to top-level props (indent ≤2) so a nested leaf descriptor (the matrix-grid per-cell `cellStyle` field — styling data, not shell appearance) is not flagged; that indent cap is what the type-agnostic pattern now leans on entirely. The `include` is an array so it catches both the `*Shell.tsx`-named page shells and the `*Sheet.tsx`-named overlay shells (e.g. crud-dialog's `CrudDialogSheet`) — a shell not named `*Shell.tsx` would otherwise slip the gate. It also carries the two `src/components/layout/**` shell/sheet globs, so a shell in the shared-chrome layer (`AppShell`) is gated on the same terms as an archetype's own; no layout-layer shell declares `className` today, the root is here so the class stays closed when one grows.

An appearance-bearing `ReactNode` slot (`header`, `stats`) is a per-call-site appearance prop by another name (RULES.md hard rule 12). The `include` carries `src/components/layout/**` as a second root because the shared chrome lives outside `src/components/archetypes/` — the same layout-layer widen as the sibling appearance rules. Pattern is optional-slot-only (`header?` / `stats?`), so a required composition slot (e.g. `AppShell`'s required `header` prop, the app's structural header region) is out of scope by design — an untyped-by-default slot the consumer must fill is structure, not a per-call-site appearance. Closed archetypes (detail-overview, form-page, list-with-detail, settings-table) are gated by their own `*-` error rules; detail-overview's typed `stats: StatItem[]` is separately gated by `detail-overview-appearance-slot`.

A **render-callback** prop — a function-typed prop returning `ReactNode` (`renderHeader?: (args) => React.ReactNode`) — is a per-call-site appearance prop wearing a function signature (RULES.md hard rule 12). It is the same unenumerable escape hatch the five sibling appearance rules ban, one level of indirection up: whatever the caller returns becomes the component's look, and no contract line derives it. The concrete instance that motivated this rule (`GroupedListSection.renderHeader`) was DELETED by `adherence-lint-appearance-slot-layout-gap`, so this rule guards a class with no live violation — the same forward-guard posture `archetype-shell-class-name` takes with its `src/components/layout/**` shell globs (no layout shell declares `className` today either). The appearance-vs-structural line is drawn by two mechanisms, matching this config's existing discipline. (1) **At the pattern**, like `archetype-appearance-slot`: the rule is OPTIONAL-only (`render…?`), so a REQUIRED render callback is out of scope by design — `Sidebar.renderLink` and `SectionNav.renderLink` are required router link-adaptors the consumer MUST supply, which is structure, not a per-call-site appearance, exactly as `AppShell`'s required `header` is structure to the slot rule. The one structural callback that is optional, `renderBackLink?` (`src/components/layout/PageHeader.tsx`, `src/components/archetypes/form-page/FormPageHeader.tsx`), is kept out by the leading negative lookahead rather than two path excludes, because it is the NAME that is structural by role — a router back-link adapter taking `(href, label)` — the same keep-the-owned-set-out-at-the-pattern move `archetype-alias-union-prop`'s lookahead makes. (2) **By path exclude**, like `archetype-alias-union-prop`'s raw-input entry: matrix-grid's `renderCell?` is contract-keyed, not discretionary — `matrix-grid.md:154` types it as the filled-cell content channel carrying `{ row, column, cell, isFilled }`; `matrix-grid.md:165` names the cell-variant axis "composition via `renderCell` / `cellStyle` — not props", making it the sanctioned alternative to an appearance prop rather than an instance of one; and `matrix-grid.md:321` hands the consumer the whole body by contract ("Consumers control the entire `renderCell` body … The shell does not constrain"). Its value is derived per cell from `ctx`, so ADR-0004's derived-not-inherited test passes. `include` carries `src/components/layout/**` as a second root because the shared chrome the archetype shells compose lives outside `src/components/archetypes/` — the same layout-layer widen as the sibling appearance rules. Closed folders are NOT excluded: no per-folder ratchet rule names a render callback, so this rule is the only gate on one. Known ceilings, deliberately left to the message rather than grown into the regex (ADR-0003 — zero-dep single-line scanner, no type resolution): the prefix scope is `render[A-Z]…` only, so a `*Render` / `on*Render` spelling is unguarded (zero instances exist); a REQUIRED appearance render-callback is out of scope, the same ceiling `archetype-appearance-slot` accepts and documents; and a declaration wrapped across lines is not seen. A path `exclude` un-gates the whole FILE, not the one legal prop — the same ceiling every per-archetype exclude in this config carries, tightened by `adherence-lint-closed-folder-allowlist-gap`, not by a second mechanism here.

detail-overview's `surface` axis is deleted — `unified` is the only container model (archetype-convergence detail-overview close-API). Re-adding it reopens the inherited-default defect (RULES.md hard rule 12).
detail-overview's `rhythm` prop is deleted — the contract sets no 'short' threshold, so nobody derives the same value (RULES.md hard rule 12).
`className` is an unenumerable superset escape hatch on the detail-overview shell — `className="border-0 shadow-none"` reconstitutes the deleted `surface="separated"` (RULES.md hard rule 12).
detail-overview's `header` / `stats` are typed data (`title`/`subtitle`/`badges`/`actions`, `stats: StatItem[]`), not appearance-bearing `ReactNode` slots (RULES.md hard rule 12).

detail-overview accepts no `headerFill` override — it is a closed project context set once at `<AppShell>`; an override next to it is the escape-hatch defect this roadmap removes (RULES.md hard rule 12).

detail-overview is closed, so its folder is excluded from the shared drain rules; this residual rule catches the appearance-shaped props they no longer reach. Any appearance prop NOT on the enumerated legal list is an error (RULES.md hard rule 12) — a new `variant` / `density` / `appearance` / a string- or numeric-literal union, etc. Enforces 2026-08-17-archetype-convergence-design.md's class-level acceptance (no further archetype-rollout-shaped ticket filable against a closed archetype's API). Legal and skipped by the leading negative lookahead: `layout` — keyed to entity density (detail-overview.md L274: `layout` "vertical|rail", dense/transactional/financial -> rail, light/early-stage -> vertical), so it derives the same value every call site; `width` — keyed to wide tables (detail-overview.md L276–277, L323–325: `width` "md" default | "none" only for wide embedded tables, ignored under `layout="rail"`), so it derives the same value; `tone` on `DetailSection` — contract-keyed to the data-section-vs-reference-panel distinction (detail-overview.md L517–519: data sections use the default tone; reference panels use `tone="muted"`), the same grading entity-circle.md L7 and calendar.md Layer 7 key their `tone` to, so ADR-0004's derived test passes and the prop is legal.

`className` is an unenumerable superset escape hatch on the form-page shell (RULES.md hard rule 12). form-page is closed: `width` is contract-keyed to field count / column layout and the shell carries no `className` prop — fork the component instead.

Re-adding it reopens the inherited-default defect (RULES.md hard rule 12).

list-with-detail's `unstyled` flush flag is deleted — the chrome-suppression decision belongs to the *composing* archetype via the internal `ListChromeContext` (mirroring detail-overview's `UnifiedSurfaceContext`), not to a per-page prop (RULES.md hard rule 12).

settings-table is closed, so its folder is excluded from the shared drain rules; this residual rule catches the appearance-shaped props they no longer reach. NO prop on the settings-table surface is a contract-keyed look (the column `align`, `isIdentifier`, and state props are data, not appearance), so there is nothing to keep on the allowlist and the pattern carries no legal-name lookahead — every appearance-shaped prop is an error (RULES.md hard rule 12): an appearance-noun, a string-literal union, or a numeric-literal union. Enforces 2026-08-17-archetype-convergence-design.md's class-level acceptance (no further archetype-rollout-shaped ticket filable against a closed archetype's API).

analytics-dashboard's grid `columns` prop is deleted — the column ladder is fixed in `<DashboardGrid>` (1 / 2 at `sm` / 3 at `lg`). A per-page column count is an appearance with no contract keying rule, and its backwards-compatible default is disqualifying on its own (RULES.md hard rule 12). Widget width is the keyed axis instead: `<DashboardWidget span>`, required and no default, per analytics-dashboard.md Layer 6's widget span keying rule.

`<StatTileRow>`'s `columns` prop is deleted — the strip derives its cell count from `React.Children.count(children)` clamped to 2–4. "Must match the number of children" is a rule the component enforces itself, not a comment on a call-site prop (RULES.md hard rule 12).
